newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed lower against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Monday in thin trading, dealers said.
"It's business as usual. The basket is still trading at seven percent below the diagonal rate and the Bank of Israel continues buying dollars to support the basket," said Guy Levi of Bank Leumi.
"The central bank had to buy $100-$120 million today," Levi added. "The shekel weakened slightly following the rise of the U.S. currency abroad."
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket rate, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for nearly two months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3530 shekels against 3.3380 on Thursday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6450 shekels against 3.6424 on Thursday.
The Bank of Israel did not set a representative rate on Friday because striking bank employees, demanding a five-day work week, closed the commercial banks in a one-day strike.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7791 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7661 on Thursday and against the mark at 1.9805 shekels against 1.9818 on Thursday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3490 shekels.
